segments.text_en: Cosmic decision and divine selection
evidence: It was time to decide destinies in heaven and on earth,
Lagash had raised the head towards heaven in large ‘me’,
Enlil looked righteously upon lord Ningirsu.
The ‘heart’ of Enlil, it is the river Tigris, did it not bring sweet water?

segments.text_en: Proclamation of Eninnu's me
evidence: To the house its king spoke:
“I will make the ‘me’ of Eninnu emerge in heaven and on earth.
The governor is wise, he shall pay attention.
The brick of deciding destinies lifted the head towards him,

segments.text_en: Ningirsu's gaze and command to build
evidence: It was then, in a ‘dark goat’, that towards his king,
on the lord Ningirsu, Gudea looked.
“Build his house!,” he ordered him.
he (Ningirsu) directed his (Gudea’s) eye there.

segments.text_en: Gudea's uncertainty and resolve to consult Nanše
evidence: Gudea, his ‘heart’ is distant,
Of what my ‘dark goat’ has revealed to me,
its ‘heart’ I did not know.
Let me bring my dream to her, to my mother.
may she make its meaning visible for me.”

segments.text_en: Voyage to Bagara and prayer to Ningirsu
evidence: Did he not set foot on his barge?
he sacrificed bread, he poured out cold water,
Ningirsu, let me build your house for you,
the lord Ningirsu, received from him.
In the House of Bagara he celebrated the week-festival.

segments.text_en: Supplication to mother-goddess Gatumdu
evidence: The governor set up his bed in the house of Gatumdu.
I am a no-mother-haver, you are my mother.
Gatumdu, your shiny name is sweet.
Let me bring my dream to my mother,
His cry was heard.

segments.text_en: Arrival at Nina and recounting the dream to Nanše
evidence: To her city, Nina, he moored at the port of Nina.
He went to Nanše, he prayed to her:
Inside the dream there was one man, his greatness was like heaven,
He spoke to me about the building of his house.
the brick of deciding destinies was placed in the mold for me.

segments.text_en: Nanše interprets the dream and gives instructions
evidence: His mother, Nanše, answered the governor:
“My shepherd, let me, me interpret your dream for you.
it is surely my brother Ningirsu.
‘Build his shrine, the Eninnu!’ He ordered you.
He will reveal the plan of his house to you.

segments.text_en: Gudea prepares chariot, emblem and harp for Ningirsu
evidence: The righteous shepherd Gudea learnt big, and now he will perform big.
He broke the seal of his treasure house,
He fashioned his beloved emblem for him,
in Eninnu, the white Anzu,
he enters.

segments.text_en: Gudea petitions Ningirsu for the missing sign
evidence: Didn’t Gudea go out, brilliantly, from the shrine Eninnu?
cedar incense, the incense of the gods,
Ningirsu, I will build your house for you,
(but) my sign is my not.
I, what can I learn from you?”

segments.text_en: Ningirsu grants the sign and promises abundance
evidence: Gudea, I will surely give you the sign of the building of my house.
The shiny star of my ‘garza’ I will certainly proclaim for you.
Its terrible radiance reaches the heaven.
I will let bounty come to you from the heaven.
On that day (when) your arm is touched with fire, I will teach you my sign.”

segments.text_en: Waking, fear, and confirming divination
evidence: Gudea rose, it was a dream.
He is afraid, it was a dream.
He struck the hand into the goat, his goat is good.
For Gudea, the ‘heart’ of Ningirsu it is the light, that dawned on him.
He learned big, and now he will perform big.

segments.text_en: Purification of the city and social ordering
evidence: The governor cleansed the city, he spun it with fire.
A mother does not accuse a son,
he made the brick appear by the goat,
The shepherd named by Nanše performed in princeliness,
in order to build the house of Ningirsu, ... they stood with him.

segments.text_en: Mustering a levy under the tribal emblems
evidence: On that day, the governor arranged a levy in his land,
In the Gu'edina of Ningirsu he placed a levy.
in the ‘tribe’ of Nanše, he made a levy for him.
The sun-disk, it is the emblem of Inanna, went at its head.

segments.text_en: Foreign lands submit and procurement is ordered
evidence: Elam came to him from Elam.
Magan and Meluhha, from their land, submitted to him.
He gave instructions to Ninzaga:
To the land of cedar, where no man enters, ... the Lord Ningirsu made way for him.

segments.text_en: Gathering of timber, stone and precious metals
evidence: He cut down its cedars with the great axe.
From the cedar mountains, cedar beams,
Its large stones, in blocks, he brought,
Purified silver is being brought down for Gudea from its mountain.
He will build Eninnu with precious stones, sitting with the stonecutter,

segments.text_en: Tireless devotion and the divine blueprint
evidence: He made the days long for him, he made the nights long for him.
It is him, the governor chosen in the ‘heart’ by Enlil,
Nisaba, the house of wisdom, she opened for him.
Enki made the plan of the house right for him.

segments.text_en: Measuring the platform and morning purification
evidence: its ‘me’ embraces heaven and earth,
the field was right, he measured it,
he placed sticks on its border, he knew himself.
Gudea, at Baragirnunata calmed his ‘heart’.

segments.text_en: Ritual making of the first brick
evidence: The shiny basket, the righteous mold of deciding destinies, he raised to Eninnu.
Gudea placed clay in the mold.
He shook the mold, he threw the brick to dry.
(About) his brick placed in the mold, Utu was pleased with it.
King Enki decided its destiny for him.

segments.text_en: Lifting the brick, omens and vigilant concern
evidence: he lifted the brick from the mold, it is a shiny throne raised to heaven.
it is Nisaba whose ‘heart’ knows counting.
he does not allow sweet sleep to enter his eyes.
he slept, the word dawned on him.
the separation of Eninnu from heaven and earth, was brought to his attention.

segments.text_en: Gods co-found the house; crown and seven blessings
evidence: He threw the flax, he perfected the me.
Enki places the foundation of the house,
The mother of Lagash, Shiny-Gatumdu, bore its bricks in flows.
he placed the basket of the house, a shiny crown, on the head,
For the seventh (time) did he not give a blessing in the house?

segments.text_en: Setting the doors; the house grows toward heaven
evidence: They place the wood of the door.
They make the house grow like a mountain.
The house raised the head to heaven like a mountain in heaven and earth.
Eninnu, brickwork of Kiengir, carries joy,

segments.text_en: Foundation, weapon-emblem and stone-working
evidence: The governor built the house, he made it grow,
he placed the very large mast, the foundation, its Abzu, in the ground.
He placed the ‘multitude-eraser’, like a great sign, with Lagash
he brought them in a single year, he worked them in a single year,
on the seventh day he seized them in the house.

segments.text_en: Erecting and naming the stelae
evidence: His stone erected in the mighty courtyard,
Lord Ningirsu, on Gudea looked righteously,
as name of that stone he named.
‘Eninnu, knowing the face of An, Baba, life of Gudea,’

segments.text_en: Completion and glorification of the house
evidence: He build the house of his king with righteousness.
Raising the crown like the new moon,
Gudea made the house of Ningirsu stand to be admired.
it is the ‘heart’ of the gods, returned to its banks.

segments.text_en: Installing guardian weapons, heroes and monstrous gates
evidence: At Šugalam, the gate of radiance, the dragon and the date palm he seizes there.
Because they are dead warriors, ... Gudea, governor of Lagash, made them emerge.
The cedar doors standing in the house, it is Iškur roaring from heaven.
The fear of Eninnu, on all the lands, like a garment, it covered.

segments.text_en: Cosmic description of the finished house and its abundance
evidence: The house, founded by Anu with purified silver,
rising in heavenly brilliance, like the moon.
From the brewery, (called) ‘Tigris is being water in its might’.
In the treasury, precious stones, silver, tin.
The fear of Eninnu covers all the lands like a garment.

segments.text_en: House built in joy and closing praise
evidence: The house (was) built in joy by its king.
Gudea, governor of Lagash, placed its foundation.
For the restoration of Eninnu Ningirsu be praised!
The building of the house of Ningirsu, this is the middle of the praise.
